title: Brian Bosworth: OU's Two-Time Butkus Award Linebacker
question: Who won the first two Butkus Awards?
answer: Oklahoma linebacker Brian Bosworth won the first two Butkus Awards, in 1985 and 1986, and remains the award's only two-time college winner.
summary: Brian Bosworth won the first two Butkus Awards in 1985 and 1986, led OU in tackles three straight years and helped win the 1985 national title.
body: When the Butkus Award debuted in 1985 to honor the nation's best college linebacker, it did not take long to find a favorite. Oklahoma City native Brian Bosworth won the very first one, then came back and won it again in 1986, becoming the award's first two-time winner.

The Boz was the heartbeat of Barry Switzer's defense from 1984 through 1986. He led the Sooners in tackles in each of his three seasons and finished with 395 career stops. His 22 tackles against Miami in 1986 set the school's single-game record. He was a consensus first-team All-American in both 1985 and 1986 and his conference's MVP both years.

The team results matched the individual ones. OU went 31-4-1 during his time in Norman, won three Big Eight titles and played in three straight Orange Bowls. In the Orange Bowl against Penn State that capped the 1985 title run, Bosworth was credited with 13 solo tackles.
He was also a serious student. Bosworth was named Academic All-America in 1986 and graduated early with a communications degree.

The Seattle Seahawks took him in the 1987 supplemental draft, and he played three seasons there. Since football he has worked in acting and real estate and founded Boz's Kids, a charity offering activities for underprivileged children in Oklahoma. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2015. Later Sooners Rocky Calmus (2001) and Teddy Lehman (2003) also brought the Butkus Award to Norman.
